newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end easier as Telecom closes on its lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end easier as Telecom closes on its lows.

text.p: * New Zealand shares end easier as Telecom retraces
* Communications minister's comments don't help Telecom
* FCL Building dips 15 cents as interest rate concerns mount ---------------------------(Mar 5)------------------------------
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
322 -1 * NZSC cap index -9.66 at 5,123.53
358 +2 * Volume NZ$72 million. Futures -1 at 1,136
668 -1 * Other movers - -15 -15
New Zealand shares eased on Wednesday after Telecom retraced from early strength to close on its lows.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 5.32 points weaker at 2,283.26, with Telecom down a cent at NZ$6.68.
The market leader traded as high as NZ$6.80 this session but comments by Communications minister Maurice Williamson took the wind from its sails, brokers said.

Williamson told a conference of telecommunications users in Wellington that phone companies needed to make faster progress on interconnection agreements for new players and number portability, or risk government intervention.
Number portability -- the ability of a phone user to retain his or her phone number when changing carrier -- is considered necessary if competitive phone services are to develop.
"If you can't fix this yourselves and if you can't negotiate through this in a commercially sensible manner, then you will give me no option," Williamson warned the major phone companies.
"So that didn't help Telecom," said Sean Vaughan at County Natwest. He said Telecom was likely to trade higher as its dividend payment, on March 19, neared.
"But I still believe it's got a lot of downside," Vaughan said.
While Fletcher Paper gained two to $2.87, Fletcher Building took a 15 cent hit to end at $4.15.
Brokers said mounting concerns that the Reserve Bank would hold a tight line in its six-monthly economic projections, due on March 13, may be undermining Building.
